get.description: Read a page of CRM objects of a specified type. You can control the data returned by specifying desired properties through query parameters. This endpoint supports pagination and can include historical property values and associations if requested.

parameters.name: after
parameters.description: The paging cursor token of the last successfully read resource will be returned as the `paging.next.after` JSON property of a paged response containing more results.

parameters.name: archived
parameters.description: Whether to return only results that have been archived.

parameters.name: associations
parameters.description: A comma separated list of object types to retrieve associated IDs for. If any of the specified associations do not exist, they will be ignored.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: The maximum number of results to display per page.

parameters.name: properties
parameters.description: A comma separated list of the properties to be returned in the response. If any of the specified properties are not present on the requested object(s), they will be ignored.

parameters.name: propertiesWithHistory
parameters.description: A comma separated list of the properties to be returned along with their history of previous values. If any of the specified properties are not present on the requested object(s), they will be ignored. Usage of this parameter will reduce the maximum number of objects that can be read by a single request.

post.description: Create a CRM object with the specified properties and return a copy of the object, including its ID. This endpoint allows you to create standard objects in your CRM system, providing documentation and examples for guidance.

Location.description: URL of the newly created resource

post.description: Archive a batch of CRM objects by their IDs. This endpoint is useful for moving multiple objects to the recycling bin in a single request, streamlining the process of managing large datasets.

Create a batch of CRM objects for a specified object type in HubSpot. This endpoint allows you to create multiple objects in a single request, which can be useful for efficiently adding large amounts of data. The response will include the created objects, each with its unique ID.

Read a batch of CRM objects by their internal IDs or unique property values. This endpoint allows you to retrieve multiple objects in a single request, which can be useful for efficiently managing large datasets. You can specify whether to include archived objects in the results.

parameters.name: archived
parameters.description: Whether to return only results that have been archived.

post.description: Update a batch of CRM objects in your HubSpot account. This endpoint allows you to modify multiple objects at once, streamlining the process of updating data. It returns a status indicating the success or failure of the operation, and can handle partial successes with detailed error information if some updates fail.

Create or update a batch of CRM objects by unique property values. This endpoint allows you to efficiently manage multiple objects in a single request, ensuring that objects are either created or updated based on their unique identifiers.

Search for CRM objects of a specified type using a variety of filters and criteria. This endpoint allows you to perform complex searches on CRM objects by specifying filter groups, sorting options, and properties to include in the results. It is useful for retrieving specific data sets from your CRM based on detailed search conditions.

get.description: Read an object identified by `{objectId}`. By default, `{objectId}` refers to the internal object ID, but it can also refer to any unique property value specified by the `idProperty` query parameter. You can control the returned data using the `properties` query parameter. This endpoint is useful for retrieving detailed information about a specific object, including its properties and associations.

parameters.name: archived
parameters.description: Whether to return only results that have been archived.

parameters.name: associations
parameters.description: A comma separated list of object types to retrieve associated IDs for. If any of the specified associations do not exist, they will be ignored.

parameters.name: idProperty
parameters.description: The name of a property whose values are unique for this object type

parameters.name: properties
parameters.description: A comma separated list of the properties to be returned in the response. If any of the specified properties are not present on the requested object(s), they will be ignored.

parameters.name: propertiesWithHistory
parameters.description: A comma separated list of the properties to be returned along with their history of previous values. If any of the specified properties are not present on the requested object(s), they will be ignored.

delete.description: Move an Object identified by `{objectId}` to the recycling bin. This operation allows you to archive a specific CRM object by its unique identifier, effectively removing it from active use but retaining it in the system for potential recovery or reference.

patch.description: Perform a partial update of an object identified by `objectId`. The `objectId` refers to the internal object ID by default, or optionally any unique property value as specified by the `idProperty` query parameter. Provided property values will be overwritten, while read-only and non-existent properties will be ignored. Properties can be cleared by passing an empty string.

parameters.name: idProperty
parameters.description: The name of a property whose values are unique for this object type

post.description: Permanently delete a contact and all associated content to comply with GDPR regulations. This endpoint allows you to specify an optional property 'idProperty' set to 'email' to identify the contact by email address. If the email address is not found, it will be added to a blocklist to prevent future use.

Merge two CRM objects of the same type in your HubSpot account. This operation combines the properties and associations of the specified objects into a single object, identified by the primary object ID.
